end.summary:
Practised speed = distance ÷ time and average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
Calculated 100 m ÷ 4 s = 25 m/s and average speed for a round trip as 40 km/h.
Practised a = (v − u)/t, including 3 m/s² for speeding up and −5 m/s² for slowing down.
Diya continued to mix up negative acceleration with deceleration and zero acceleration; this was not fully corrected by the end.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: They used the braking example to obtain −5 m/s² and the starting-from-rest example to obtain 3 m/s². The mix-up between negative acceleration, deceleration, and zero acceleration remained at the end, although they repeated that changing velocity gives acceleration.
